structured_output.summary:
Phase 5 (Model Security and Red Team) meets its acceptance criteria with independently verifiable evidence. All 151 frozen baseline methods in the `src/model-security/` and `src/red-team/` families are implemented and mapped with no deferrals: `contracts/operations.json` contains exactly 151 methods for those two source trees, `contracts/native-operations.json` marks all 151 with `owningPhase: 5`, `implementation: implemented`, `contractVerification: offline_fixture_verified`, and `python tools/native_operations.py --check --require-through-phase 5` passed (implemented 250, pending 198, completeMethodOptionParity 248 — the 2 partials are Phase-6-owned Gateway slices). I independently recounted the baseline per client against `.local/typescript` (scans 14, models 8, security-groups 10, security-rules 4, custom-rules 12, PyPI 1 = 49; red-team facade 13, scans 6, reports 14, custom-attack-reports 7, instances 8 = 48; custom-attacks 22, targets 16, adapters 8, broker 5, EULA 3 = 54) and every route, HTTP method, query key, query order, request/response schema name, and default I spot-checked matches the frozen source exactly (including `validate=true` adapter default vs. omitted target default, `adapter_uuid` UUID assertion parity, PATCH for channel updates, POST `/v1/metering/quota` with a separate GET summary, and the `file_format`/`prompt_set_uuid` query names).

Test evidence is real and executed, not claimed: 17 model-security, 12 red-team and 20 red-team-resources hand-authored contract tests ran and passed under `--features model-security`, `--features red-team`, and `--features all` on both 1.88.0 (MSRV) and 1.99.0, per the recorded per-feature child reports. The tests assert literal URLs per plane, exact ordered query pairs, exact header name sets and sensitivity, exact JSON request bytes, and round-trip equality against response bodies, with unconsumed-fixture and call-count assertions that would catch a replay. The 38 Red Team direct fixtures are byte-identical copies of two manifest-pinned independent OpenAPI fixtures, checked by `tools/verify_native_fixtures.py` against recorded SHA256 plus JSON-pointer coordinates, with 9 tamper-rejection tests. Mutation safety is strong: 14 + 12 + 26 = 52 mutation paths are proven single-dispatch with `RemoteOutcome::Unknown` even with a retry override of 5. Pagination matches `collectSkipPages` semantics exactly while adding explicit truncation, byte/page/item caps, resumable positions, retained rows on rejected opaque cursors, and the conservative latched `count_capped` cursor; CSV multipart bytes, forced `prompts.csv` filename, MIME default, non-UTF-8 preservation and Fetch-style text decoding are all byte-asserted. Security posture is sound: OAuth-only constructors, `x-tsg-id` omission matching the baseline, admitted-destination endpoint rebinding, pre-authentication identifier/query/body rejection, redacted `Debug` on every option type, no `unsafe`, and no `unwrap`/`panic` in product paths.

No functional, security or contract-completeness defect was found. The deductions are maintainability and record-precision items, the most notable being that the phase-4 advisory to expand compressed whitespace/macro formatting is only partially closed and `cargo fmt --check` does not actually enforce the over-long lines that remain.

findings.description: `RedTeamClient::get_scan_metadata` validates against SID `s012087`, which `contracts/typescript.json:371958` confirms is `ZodRecord(ZodString unconstrained, ZodUnknown)` — the exact shape of `targets-client.ts` `getTargetMetadata`'s `z.record(z.unknown())`. However the frozen facade route's own inline contract is `z.object({}).passthrough()` (`.local/typescript/src/red-team/client.ts:98`), a different Zod kind. The two are behaviourally equivalent for JSON (both accept any object, reject arrays/null/scalars, preserve all keys), so this is not a wire defect, but the recorded justification in `contracts/native-operation-mappings/red-team.json:164` and the inline comment at facade.rs:107-108 assert structural equivalence without naming the facade's actual schema kind, so a future reviewer cannot re-derive the claim the way they can for `targets.rs:11-14`.
findings.required_fix: Record the facade route's actual frozen schema kind (`ZodObject` with passthrough) alongside the reused `s012087` SID in `contracts/native-operation-mappings/red-team.json` and in the facade.rs comment, and state explicitly why ZodObject-passthrough and ZodRecord(string, unknown) accept and emit the same JSON objects.

findings.description: New Phase 5 production code introduces a 173-character single-line `macro_rules! redacted_debug` with no spaces around tokens. More broadly, the phase-4 review advisory recorded in docs/phase-status.json:256 as "implementation_in_phase_5" ("expand whitespace/macro formatting") is only partially closed: 45 lines longer than 120 characters remain in the three Phase 5 test files (red_team_resources_contracts.rs 19, model_security_contracts.rs 16, red_team_contracts.rs 10), including unformatted statements such as `let errors=[` at red_team_resources_contracts.rs:1882-1909 and the compressed macro bodies at management_contracts.rs:716-717. These survive because there is no `rustfmt.toml` in the repository, so rustfmt silently leaves statements it cannot fit inside the default 100-column `max_width` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` reports success — the recorded formatting check therefore does not enforce these lines at all.
findings.required_fix: Expand the `redacted_debug!` definition across multiple lines, reformat the remaining over-long statements (JSON literals excepted), and add a `rustfmt.toml` setting `error_on_line_overflow = true` (or an explicit `max_width`) so the recorded `cargo fmt --check` evidence actually binds the formatting claim.

findings.description: The redaction `Debug` impl is hand-written and duplicated for essentially every option type: 20 copies in model_security/query.rs and 13 more across the red_team modules (facade.rs 2, custom_attacks.rs 2, reports.rs 2, targets.rs 2, adapters.rs 3, scans.rs 1, network_broker.rs 1, common.rs 1), while a `redacted_debug!` macro that generates exactly this impl already exists but is applied to only 3 types in custom_attack_reports.rs:32-37. Each hand-written copy is a place where a future option type can silently omit redaction, which is a security-relevant invariant rather than cosmetic boilerplate.
findings.required_fix: Hoist the `redacted_debug!` macro into a crate-internal module and apply it to all Phase 5 option types, so redaction is a single declaration per type and a missing impl is visible at a glance.

findings.description: `send_text` (used by `red_team::custom_attacks::download_template`) wraps the decode in `options.run(...)` at lines 981-990 and then immediately wraps the already-produced `String` in a second `options.run(&self.inner.session, async { Ok(text) })` at lines 991-995. If this exists to re-observe deadline/cancellation after decoding, that intent is undocumented; if not, it is dead work on every text response.
findings.required_fix: Either remove the second `options.run` wrapper or add a one-line comment stating that the operation budget and cancellation are deliberately re-checked after decoding, matching the commenting discipline used elsewhere in engine.rs.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-05.json records 33 commands, all exit_code 0, with source_sha256 ebffaeb5a6d6e38a2b93f317f3989e9424eb4c86025acad9d369884cbd177c3d matching the reviewed source SHA, source_unchanged true and passed true. The 33 commands exactly reconstruct tools/check_phase.py commands_for(5) (7 phase-1 + 19 phase-3 + 3 phase-4 + 4 phase-5), so the recorded set is the complete bound set, not a subset.

Contract completeness: `rg -c '"id": "src/model-security/|"id": "src/red-team/' contracts/operations.json` = 151; `"owningPhase": 5` in contracts/native-operations.json = 151; all 151 also match `implementation: implemented` + `contractVerification: offline_fixture_verified`; the three Phase 5 mapping fragments total 151 `baselineId` entries (model-security 49, red-team 48, red-team-resources 54), all `deliveredInPhase: 5`.

tools/native_operations.py:94-104 enforces that every mapped native method exists as `pub [async] fn <name>(` in its declared source file and that every referenced test function name exists in an existing test file, and tools/test_native_operations.py's 10 tests (all passed, recorded stderr) include test_removed_native_method_is_rejected, test_absent_verification_function_is_rejected, test_invented_frozen_operation_is_rejected and test_completed_owning_phase_rejects_an_unimplemented_operation.

Independent per-client recount against the frozen baseline: `rg '^  async [a-zA-Z]+' .local/typescript/src/model-security` yields 49 methods (custom-rules 12, scans 14, models 8, security-rules 4, client 1, security-groups 10), matching the 49 Rust methods in crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/model_security/*.rs; red-team yields 48 + 54 = 102, matching docs/phase-status.json implemented_scope.

Executed test counts from the recorded child reports: docs/checks/phase-05-rust-1.99.0-model-security.json shows `running 17 tests ... 17 passed`; phase-05-rust-1.99.0-red-team.json shows `running 12 tests ... 12 passed` and `running 20 tests ... 20 passed`; phase-05-rust-1.88.0-all.json shows 17, 12 and 20 again on the MSRV toolchain. Under `--features scan` and `--features gateway` those same binaries correctly report `running 0 tests`, confirming the counts come from feature-gated execution rather than double counting.

crates/scm-sdk/tests/model_security_contracts.rs:92-132 asserts the per-plane base URL, exact method, the full ordered `Vec<(String,String)>` of query pairs, the exact sorted header name set with `headers.len()` equality, bearer value, `is_sensitive()`, `service-name: api`, the Rust User-Agent, and exact JSON request bytes; tests/model_security_contracts.rs:441-561 drives all 8 model methods against literal `/v1/models`, `/v1/models/{id}/model-versions`, `/v1/model-versions/{id}` and `/v1/model-versions/{id}/files` routes and ends with `wire.done()`.

Mutation no-replay: tests/model_security_contracts.rs:1216-1344 drives all 14 model-security mutations through a transport failure and asserts `(ErrorKind::Transport, RemoteOutcome::Unknown)` with `wire.calls == 14`; tests/red_team_resources_contracts.rs:1874-1919 does the same for all 26 resource mutations with `RequestOptions::with_retries(5)` and asserts exactly 26 dispatches plus the absence of four distinct secret strings in `Debug`/`Display`; tests/red_team_contracts.rs:981 covers the 12 facade/scans/reports/instances mutations.

Frozen fixture provenance: crates/scm-sdk/src/fixtures/red-team-contracts.json pins contracts/fixtures/typescript/test/openapi/fixtures/redteam-data.json (dc29f182...) and redteam-management.json (5fb99c07...); tools/verify_native_fixtures.py:49-85 re-hashes each source, requires the manifest category `independent-openapi-fixture`, and requires each case to be canonically identical to its `/cases/N` pointer. Recorded output: {"bundles": 1, "exact_frozen_cases": 38}; tests/red_team_contracts.rs:293-493 then replays all 38 through the public clients and asserts `wire.count() == 38` with a `panic!("uncovered frozen method")` arm.

Pagination semantics verified against the frozen helper: crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/common.rs:77-106 reproduces .local/typescript/src/listing.ts:88-105 `collectSkipPages` exactly (empty page terminal, `items.len() == limit` fallback when total is absent, `next < total` otherwise), and crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/model_security/mod.rs:72-82 does the same for the model-security dialect. tests/model_security_contracts.rs:1346-1486 proves the `count_capped` latch across a full page and a serialized mid-page resume, and rejects `{"skip":u64::MAX}` on deserialization.

Cursor-limit advisory from docs/reviews/phase-04-attempt-01.json implemented: crates/scm-sdk/src/pagination.rs:380-389 returns the page with its actual rows and defers the error, and pagination.rs:303-311 provides the explicit `with_cursor_limits` override; the corresponding tests (`rejected_next_cursor_retains_rows_and_can_resume_with_larger_bounds`, `cursor_values_and_retained_history_have_independent_bounds`, `rejected_cursor_errors_remain_visible_at_collection_limits`) appear in the recorded passing unit-test output.

CSV/multipart/binary evidence: tests/red_team_resources_contracts.rs:995-1088 asserts the exact multipart envelope bytes (single `file` part, forced `prompts.csv` filename, supplied `text/csv` and the `application/octet-stream` default, NUL and 0xFF bytes preserved), the single `prompt_set_uuid` query pair, one occurrence of each header, locally generated boundary, and Fetch-style text decoding (`\xef\xbb\xbf` BOM stripped, malformed byte to U+FFFD). crates/scm-sdk/src/multipart.rs:109-141 scans every part's bytes and headers for the chosen boundary before selecting it and re-checks the encoded size against `max_bytes`.

Request-bound and destination safety: crates/scm-sdk/src/config.rs:9 `MAX_URL_BYTES = 16 * 1024`, config.rs:64-71 rejects `query.len() > 256` and oversized paths centrally, config.rs:112 re-checks the fully encoded URL; model_security/query.rs:14-26 adds a pre-authentication allocation budget; engine.rs:410-418 `with_tsg_header` and engine.rs:451-471 `require_auth` back the OAuth-only, header-omitting constructors, and tests/red_team_resources_contracts.rs:1922-1948 proves all five resource constructors reject `Authentication::None`, scan and runtime-key credentials.

Duration-coincidence check: the outer report lists 80.899s for both the `scan` and `gateway` check-rust steps, but docs/checks/phase-05-rust-1.99.0-scan.json (checkedAt 13:35:16Z, step durations 1.345/13.31/15.569/29.69/20.884 = 80.798) and -gateway.json (checkedAt 13:39:39Z, 1.346/13.378/15.477/29.401/21.199 = 80.801) are distinct, independently timed runs with distinct test binaries and output, so the identical outer figure is a genuine coincidence rather than a copied record.

`rg 'todo!|unimplemented!|panic!|unsafe|unwrap\(\)' crates/scm-sdk/src/airs` matches only three lines inside an existing `scan/content.rs` unit test, confirming no placeholder or panicking paths in the Phase 5 product code.
limitations: Read-only review with no command execution: I could not re-run cargo, the Python gates or the TypeScript extractors, and could not recompute the SHA256 values for docs/checks/phase-05.json or the source tree. The passing-check claims are verified by reading the recorded command set, exit codes, stdout/stderr and the per-feature child reports, and by confirming the recorded command set is exactly the set tools/check_phase.py binds for phase 5 — not by independent re-execution.

No git access, so I could not diff Phase 5 against the accepted phase-4 source snapshot. Judgements about which phase-4 advisories were newly implemented versus pre-existing (dashboard query ordering, DLP header documentation, IAM feature dependency) rest on the current state satisfying the advisory, not on an observed change.

The machine gate in tools/native_operations.py verifies that each mapped Rust method name exists in its declared file and that each referenced test function name exists, but not that the named test actually invokes the mapped method. I closed that gap manually for the large per-family tests (which drive every method against literal fixtures and assert call counts plus `wire.done()`), but per-method test coverage for the 151 operations is established by inspection rather than by an automated assertion.

I compared routes, methods, query keys and ordering, request/response schema names and defaults against the frozen TypeScript for every client in both families, but field-by-field body-schema equivalence for all generated request/response models was taken from the existing generation and schema-oracle gates (1086 public schemas, 27216 typed cases, 60271 oracle JSON cases) rather than re-derived here.

Live service acceptance is unverified and explicitly deferred: contracts/native-operations.json records liveVerified 0 and every Phase 5 operation as `liveAcceptance: unverified`, and docs/phase-status.json sets live_acceptance to pending_phase_8. Passing offline fixtures establish the implemented wire contract only, not tenant permissions, licensing or backend availability.

Per instruction I did not read any credential or tenant-registration files and did not perform network calls, so the example's environment-variable credential reads in crates/scm-sdk/examples/model_and_red_team.rs were assessed only for consistency with the already-accepted examples/management.rs pattern.

Platform coverage in the evidence is Linux x86_64-unknown-linux-musl only, consistent with the still-open `native-platform-qualification` limitation recorded for Phase 2 and due in Phase 8; I verified no additional target or runtime evidence for Phase 5.
